titre: The Court-Appointed Lawyer Was Born of a Charter, Not a Lawsuit
accroche: In 1913, the Los Angeles County charter creates a free public defender's office, half a century before the Supreme Court imposes the idea on the whole country.
contenu_vulgarise:
In September 1878, Clara Shortridge Foltz becomes the first woman admitted to the California bar, after getting a law passed, the “Woman Lawyer Bill,” that replaced the phrase “white male” in the code with “person.” Fifteen years later, in 1893, she presents her idea at a congress organized by the Board of Lady Managers at the World's Fair in Chicago: if the state employs a paid prosecutor to bring charges, it must also pay a lawyer to defend those who cannot afford one.

It takes the idea twenty years to win out at home. In 1913, the Los Angeles County charter provides, among many other provisions, for the creation of the post of “Public Defender,” a lawyer salaried by the public body and charged with defending indigent defendants free of charge; the county board of supervisors approves the concrete plan in October 1913. The office opens in January 1914: the board appoints Walton J. Wood the first holder of the post in the United States, with four deputies and a secretary as its entire staff.

## An Office, Not a Favor

What Los Angeles County establishes is not occasional help but a permanent office, a mirror image of the prosecutor's. A study conducted by Wood himself, in 1916, shows that the acquittals and probation terms won by the new office already exceed those of the unpaid court-appointed lawyers it replaces. In 1921, California allows its nine largest counties to set up an elected public defender; Los Angeles, already equipped with an office by its charter, has no need to use it, and the smaller counties go on relying on unpaid appointed lawyers for decades.

## What the Date Shifts

The reflex, on hearing about court-appointed lawyers in the United States, is to think of Gideon v. Wainwright, the 1963 ruling in which the Supreme Court requires every state to provide a lawyer to any indigent defendant in a criminal case. Yet Los Angeles already had a salaried, functioning public defender's office forty-nine years earlier, without any court imposing it. It was not a court decision that created the right to a free defense in this part of the country; it was a county charter, carried for twenty years by a lawyer who had had to fight to practice her own profession. Gideon did not invent the public defender: it made mandatory, in all fifty states, what one California county had already been practicing for a generation.

repere.texte: Since its creation in 1914, under the impetus of Clara Shortridge Foltz, the Los Angeles County Public Defender's office has defended indigent defendants free of charge, nearly fifty years before the Supreme Court imposed the practice on the whole country with Gideon v. Wainwright (1963).

carte.punch: The free lawyer existed 49 years before the law required one.
carte.idee: In 1913, the Los Angeles County charter creates a free public defender's office, championed for twenty years by lawyer Clara Shortridge Foltz. It opens in 1914, forty-nine years before the Supreme Court requires court-appointed counsel nationwide with Gideon v. Wainwright.

pour_aller_plus_loin.titre: Gideon v. Wainwright: overview of the 1963 ruling
pour_aller_plus_loin.note: The ruling that extends to the entire United States what Los Angeles had been practicing since 1914.

quiz.question: Why is the Los Angeles public defender's office, created in 1913, surprising?
choix: Because it was funded by a private collection organized by volunteer lawyers
Because it defended only defendants facing the death penalty
Because it predates by several decades the ruling that imposes court-appointed lawyers across the country
Because the federal government immediately copied it for military courts
quiz.explication: The office opens in 1914 under the county charter of 1913, forty-nine years before Gideon v. Wainwright (1963), which requires court-appointed lawyers in all states; it was neither funded by a private collection nor limited to capital cases, and no immediate federal copying is attested.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What law did Clara Shortridge Foltz get passed so she could be admitted to the California bar in 1878?
choix: The Public Defender Act, which created a salaried lawyer's post
The Bar Admission Act, which opened the bar exam to women graduates
The Woman Lawyer Bill, which replaced “white male” with “person” in the code
The Equal Practice Bill, which authorized women to plead before all courts
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Foltz got the Woman Lawyer Bill passed, which replaced the phrase “white male” with “person” in the code, thereby opening the bar to women.

quiz_supplementaire.question: According to the study conducted by Walton J. Wood in 1916, how does the new office compare to the old system?
choix: It costs the county three times more than the old system of appointed lawyers
It already wins more acquittals and probation terms than the unpaid appointed lawyers
It achieves results identical to those of the unpaid appointed lawyers
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Wood's 1916 study shows that the new office already wins more acquittals and probation terms than the old unpaid system.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What did the 1921 California law change for the state's nine largest counties?
choix: It abolished the public defender's post created by Los Angeles in 1913
It transferred the funding of all public defenders' offices to the federal government
It forbade smaller counties from continuing to use unpaid appointed lawyers
It allowed them to set up an elected public defender; Los Angeles, which already had one by charter, had no need to use it
quiz_supplementaire.explication: In 1921, California allows its nine largest counties to set up an elected public defender; Los Angeles, which already has an office created by its 1913 charter, has no need to use it.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What was the staff of the public defender's office when it opened in January 1914?
choix: Walton J. Wood, four deputies, and a secretary
Walton J. Wood and ten deputies
Walton J. Wood alone, with no deputies
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The board of supervisors appoints Walton J. Wood the country's first public defender, with four deputies and a secretary as his entire staff.
